items.title: 5 St Andrew's Eve Love Spells
items.hook: Tomorrow night, girls once summoned their future husbands
items.angle: A countdown of real St Andrew's Eve love divinations from Poland, Romania and Germany, posted the day before the Eve so followers can try one.
items.why_now: St Andrew's Eve is the night of 29 November, tomorrow.
facts: St Andrew's Eve is the night of 29–30 November; in Poland it is called Andrzejki
Polish girls poured hot wax through the eye of a key into cold water and read their future from its shadow
Shoes were lined up from the wall to the door; the owner of the first to cross the threshold would marry first
In Romania, garlic was hung on doors and windows that night to keep away strigoi, the restless dead
Romanian girls slept with basil under their pillow to dream of their future husband
In German lands, girls prayed to St Andrew on Andreasnacht to see their future husband in a dream
items.question: Would you try one tomorrow night?

items.title: The Forbidden Library No. 2: The Voynich Manuscript
items.hook: A 600-year-old book no one can read
items.angle: Detailed breakdown of MS 408 held at Yale University's Beinecke Library.
items.why_now: Aligns with top historical archive interest.
facts: Held by Yale's Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library as MS 408
Its vellum was radiocarbon dated in 2009 to between 1404 and 1438
About 240 pages survive, written in a script no one has read
Its illustrations show plants botanists cannot identify, bathing women and star charts
The book dealer Wilfrid Voynich bought it in Italy in 1912
Cryptographers including William Friedman, who broke Japanese codes, failed to decipher it
items.question: Can you decode a single glyph?

items.title: The Necromancy Rite Hidden in The Odyssey
items.hook: The Odyssey contains a step-by-step rite for raising the dead
items.angle: Nolan's The Odyssey is in cinemas; Book 11, the Nekyia, gives Homer's exact ritual for calling up the dead.
items.why_now: The Odyssey (2026 film) is one of the most-read Wikipedia articles this week.
facts: Book 11 of Homer's Odyssey, the Nekyia, describes Odysseus calling up the dead
The witch-goddess Circe gives him the instructions
He digs a pit about a cubit wide and pours milk and honey, then wine, then water, and sprinkles white barley
He sacrifices a ram and a black ewe, and the dead gather to drink the blood
The ghosts can speak to him only after drinking the blood
He holds the others back with his sword until the prophet Tiresias has drunk and foretold his journey home
items.question: Would you go down to the underworld for an answer?

items.title: Find Your Sign's Herb in Culpeper's Herbal
items.hook: A 1652 herbal assigns a herb to your sign
items.angle: Culpeper gave every herb a ruling planet; follow your sign's classical ruler to its herb.
items.why_now: Timed with the Last Quarter Moon in Virgo on 2026-12-01 06:08 UTC.
facts: Nicholas Culpeper published The English Physitian in 1652, naming a ruling planet for each herb
Classical rulers: Aries and Scorpio, Mars; Taurus and Libra, Venus; Gemini and Virgo, Mercury; Cancer, the Moon; Leo, the Sun; Sagittarius and Pisces, Jupiter; Capricorn and Aquarius, Saturn
Culpeper calls garlic and wormwood herbs of Mars
Mugwort and vervain he gives to Venus; valerian to Mercury; lettuce to the Moon
St John's wort and rosemary he places under the Sun; sage under Jupiter; comfrey under Saturn
Culpeper wrote in English so ordinary people could treat themselves without paying physicians
items.question: What's your sign, and do you grow its herb?

items.title: The Occult Roots of Queen Victoria's Mourning
items.hook: Victoria wore black for 40 years. Her age called up the dead
items.angle: Victoria's endless mourning and the Victorian craze for séances; separates the documented history from the legend that she contacted Albert.
facts: Prince Albert died on 14 December 1861
Queen Victoria wore mourning black from then until her death in 1901
Modern Spiritualism began in 1848 with the Fox sisters' rappings in Hydesville, New York
Séances became a fashionable entertainment in Victorian drawing rooms
The medium D. D. Home held séances for Napoleon III and Empress Eugénie
Stories that Victoria contacted Albert through a medium are legend, not documented
items.question: Have you ever attended a séance?

items.title: 4 Lies You Believe About Medieval Witch Trials
items.hook: Most of what you know about witch trials is wrong
items.angle: Deconstructing modern misconceptions versus actual inquisitorial court records.
facts: The great witch hunts were early modern, peaking about 1560–1660, not medieval
The Malleus Maleficarum was written by Heinrich Kramer and first printed in 1486
In England convicted witches were hanged, not burned
At Salem in 1692, 19 people were hanged and Giles Corey was pressed to death; none were burned
In Iceland most of those executed for witchcraft were men
The Holy Roman Empire's Carolina law code of 1532 required evidence before torture could be used
items.question: Which myth did you fall for?

items.title: Krampus Comes Tomorrow Night
items.hook: Tomorrow night the Krampus comes for bad children
items.angle: A countdown of the Krampus tradition on the eve of Krampusnacht.
facts: Krampus is a horned, hairy demon of Alpine folklore who travels with St Nicholas
Krampusnacht is 5 December, the eve of St Nicholas' Day
St Nicholas rewards good children while Krampus punishes bad ones
He carries birch switches and rattling chains, and sometimes a basket to carry children off
In Krampus runs, men in carved wooden masks and sheepskins parade through Alpine towns
Krampus greeting cards, 'Gruß vom Krampus', were popular from the late 1800s
items.question: Were you told about the Krampus as a child?
